what_this_is: Six terms were held back from the vendor blocklist. Each is a commercial company or product name that is also an ordinary English word. A case-insensitive rule on any of them would replace ordinary prose with [product], so they are not scrubbed. This file documents the resulting gap in safeguard S2 so that it is visible rather than implicit.
literal_terms_location: data/raw/vendor_terms_ordinary_word_brands.txt, which is not committed. The terms are company names, and publishing them here would put vendor names into the repository, which is the thing S2 exists to prevent.
why_the_terms_are_not_listed_here: Naming them would breach the safeguard this file documents. The category and the evidence below are enough to understand the size and shape of the gap without reproducing the names.
recheck_required: If the source data is ever re-downloaded, every term below must be re-checked in context. The conclusions here describe this file at this hash and do not carry forward automatically.

terms.semantic_category: a word for a location or a place, also used for a web page
terms.reason_held_back: Appears constantly in ordinary prose about web pages and physical locations.
terms.what_it_actually_refers_to_here: Every occurrence I checked is an internal agency system carrying this as its name, written in capitals. One entry describes the system being trained on a human-verified dataset and another describes its outputs informing analysis. None refers to the commercial company.
Occurrences are ordinary phrases. One names an assistant after a figure of speech about a doctor in a container, another describes a workflow container. None refers to the commercial company.

terms.semantic_category: a word meaning a watchman or guard
terms.what_it_actually_refers_to_here: Every occurrence refers to a European space agency's satellite programme, as a source of earth-observation imagery and radar data. That is a public science programme, not a commercial supplier.

terms.semantic_category: a word meaning a tool or person that locates things
terms.what_it_actually_refers_to_here: The single occurrence is an internal agency system, written in capitals, described as sifting violent crime and firearms trace data. Not the commercial product.

terms.semantic_category: a word meaning pleasant or agreeable
terms.what_it_actually_refers_to_here: Does not appear in this register in any form.

terms.semantic_category: a compound word meaning a day of work
terms.what_it_actually_refers_to_here: Does not appear in this register in any form.

summary_of_the_gap: Of the six, four appear in the register and none of those four carries a commercial meaning: two are internal agency system names written in capitals, one is a public satellite programme, and one appears only in ordinary figures of speech. Two do not appear at all. The documented hole is real in principle, because a future commercial mention of any of these names would pass unscrubbed, but no such mention exists in the data as downloaded.
contrast: Three further ordinary-word brand names were checked the same way, found to carry genuine commercial mentions, and returned to the blocklist. One of those was a company domain sitting inside a link. The distinction between the two groups was made from evidence in context, not from the shape of the word.
